what: Axon makes the Taser and the body cameras police officers wear, and the Evidence.com software that stores and manages the footage. The hardware is the way in; the software subscription is the business.
customers: Police departments and other law enforcement agencies, plus federal agencies, corrections, and increasingly private security and retail.
money: body cameras, in-car video, drones and Evidence.com subscriptions
moat: An agency's entire evidence workflow runs on its software, with multi-year contracts, so replacing it means retraining officers and migrating years of footage.
risks: It reported an operating loss after large stock-based compensation charges
Government budget cycles determine when agencies buy
The shares trade at a very high multiple of revenue
Public scrutiny of policing technology can slow adoption
opportunities: Revenue grew about 33% last year and about 33% a year over three years
Analysts see large upside, with a median target well above the current price
Drones, licence plate readers and AI report writing extend it well beyond cameras
watch: Annual recurring revenue and the contracted future bookings balance.
